narrative.overview:
Starfish sells proof, and the interface behaves like the room where proof is kept: dark, quiet, and exact. Every element is a labelled exhibit. The page is a near-black vault; content sits on graphite slate panels separated by 1px hairlines; a single Signal Green marks what is live, confirmed, or actionable. Nothing glows for decoration — when something lights up, it is because it is the finding, the status, or the next step. The mood is forensic, composed, exacting.

The system inherits a hacker/terminal lineage (monospace labels, a pulsing status dot, a hero transcript with a blinking caret) but disciplines it into enterprise credibility. The terminal is Exhibit A — it appears once in the hero and once as the footer mantra, and it is not a general-purpose motif. Layout is generous and grid-true: a 1152px container, long section rhythm, cards in dense 16px grids, and fluid type that stays tight at every viewport. Density is low-to-moderate; whitespace does the persuading, mono type does the labelling, and the one accent does the pointing.

Confirmed rejections carried from the owner's brief and the shipped code: no light theme in v1; no glitch effects, matrix rain, or neon saturation beyond the single accent; no serif type anywhere (the wordmark is now typeset in the site's sans); no stock imagery or fake photography — avatars are monograms until real headshots exist.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only: one near-black vault (vault-black) with two graphite lifts and hairline borders.
One chromatic voice — Signal Green — reserved for status, proof, and the primary action.
Inter for everything readable; JetBrains Mono strictly for labels, IDs, numerals, and transcript.
Depth by tone and hairline, never by neutral drop shadow; green glows respond to state.
Fluid clamp() type with −0.02em tracking on every headline size.
Motion is a 16px rise over 0.5s, staggered 80ms, once; all of it collapses under prefers-reduced-motion.
Missing data is shown as a dashed amber TodoNote, never hidden or faked.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Green is the only accent on any screen and appears on a small fraction of it: one primary button per viewport, labels, the status dot, and hover states. If a screen has two green fills competing, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Labelled Severity Rule
rules.body: Red, orange, and amber never appear outside a badge or an error message, and never without a text label beside them. Color alone is not evidence.

rules.name: The Text-on-Green Rule
rules.body: Anything set on a Signal Green fill uses Vault Black text (text-bg). White on green fails contrast and is not used.

rules.name: The Mono Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks things that are data: labels, IDs, numerals, dates, handles, email addresses, the transcript, and the mantra. It is never used for sentences a buyer reads — no mono paragraphs, no mono headings.

rules.name: The Last Word Rule
rules.body: The gradient wash lands on exactly one word of the hero headline (the last), and on stat numerals. No other running text is gradient-filled.

rules.name: The No-Serif Rule
rules.body: No serif face appears anywhere, including the wordmark, which is typeset "Starfish" in Chalk + "Sec" in Signal Green using Inter 600 at 1.02rem.

rules.name: The Glow-On-State Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A green glow appears only as a response — hover on a card or button, the hero exhibit, the featured service, the Final CTA. Never stack a resting glow on a non-featured card.

rules.name: The Masked Motif Rule
rules.body: Grid and dot backgrounds are always masked to a radial falloff and sit at ≤ 9% opacity. A full-bleed, unmasked grid is not this system.

dos: Do build every color, radius, and type size from the @theme tokens in app/globals.css (bg-bg, text-accent, rounded-card, text-h1…). There is no tailwind.config.ts; the token block is the single source of truth.
Do reserve Signal Green for one primary action per viewport plus labels, status, and hover states (The One Signal Rule), and always set Vault Black text on a green fill.
Do open sections with SectionHeading — a // eyebrow, a −0.02em headline, an optional muted subtitle — and keep 80/112/128px section padding with a hairline top border.
Do convey depth with tone and 1px hairlines; let green glows appear only on hover, on the hero exhibit, on the featured service, and on the Final CTA panel.
Do use JetBrains Mono for data only: labels, CVE IDs, numerals, dates, handles, email, transcript, mantra.

Do keep motion to the shipped grammar — Reveal (16px rise, 0.5s, ease-out-soft, once, 80ms stagger), 200ms color transitions, 1–2px hover rises under motion-safe: — and make sure prefers-reduced-motion yields the final state with no animation.
Do mask every grid/dot background to a radial falloff at ≤ 9% Chalk and clip decorative glows inside their card (overflow-hidden).
Do show pending owner data as a TodoNote; use monogram avatars (signal-green-dim fill, mono initials, gradient-ring) until real headshots exist.
Do pair every severity hue with its text label, in a badge or an error message.
donts: Don't introduce a light theme, neutral drop shadows on resting cards, or a second accent hue.
Don't add terminal chrome, blinking carets, or scanlines outside the hero exhibit and footer mantra — the terminal is Exhibit A, not a theme.
Don't use glitch effects, matrix rain, neon outlines, or saturate the accent beyond signal-green / its 12% dim.
Don't set body copy, headings, or buttons in monospace, and don't introduce any serif face — including for the wordmark.
Don't gradient-fill running text; the wash belongs to the hero's last word and stat numerals only.

Don't hardcode hex values, rounded-xl/rounded-lg, or arbitrary font sizes in components when a token utility exists; the one-off sizes inside the terminal, badges, and TodoNote are the sanctioned exceptions.
Don't lock the hero to viewport height or let any wide element (tables, the mantra) widen the page — wide content scrolls inside its own rounded, hairline-bordered shell.
Don't ship animation that depends on hydration for above-the-fold content; hero entrances are CSS-only (animate-fade-up), and [data-reveal] content must render visible without JS.
